name: Memory Maze
ability_definition: The ability to remember information such as words, numbers, pictures, and procedures.

task_realism.reasoning: The agent navigates a randomly generated 3D maze and collects colored objects in a set order, so it must remember where objects are, how rooms connect and where it is. This loosely resembles remembering a physical layout, such as a warehouse, hospital floor or building route. However, most workplace memorization is recalling words, numbers, names, codes, instructions and procedures. A toy maze-foraging game is far from these tasks.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Memory is inferred indirectly from episode reward in a reinforcement-learning setup trained for about 100M environment steps on the same task distribution. There is no clean exposure, removal, delay and recall structure. Performance is still partly mixed up with exploration, control and perception, even though the design reduces these. Real work involves little or no practice on the specific material, meaningful delays and interruptions, and stakes. None of these are present here.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark covers only spatial and visual memory: object positions, maze topology and self-location. It does not test memory for words, numbers or procedures, which are three of the four content types in the O*NET definition. It also does not separate short-term from long-term retention, and it does not test verbatim recall.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are low-resolution first-person pixel observations, outputs are discrete movement actions, and the score is a reward count. None of these resemble workplace artifacts such as lists, documents, figures or checklists. Nor do they resemble how memory is used at work, for example reciting a procedure or recalling a number.

transferability_reasoning: Memory Maze is a well-designed test of long-horizon spatial memory in reinforcement-learning agents, but it captures only a narrow visuospatial slice of Memorization. It works through an artificial navigation-and-reward format. Its tasks, conditions and artifacts differ greatly from workplace recall of words, numbers and procedures, so benchmark gains would say little about real on-the-job memorization capability.

2022.metric: mean episode return on Memory Maze 15x15 (number of prompted targets reached per 4,000-step episode; human baseline about 67.7)
2022.human_reference: General adult population doing a spatial and visual memory navigation task. This is the typical person who has to remember locations, object positions and layouts in work settings.
